prompt:
Investigating pressure, mechanical work, and acoustic wave speed in a gas cylinder.
(a) Pressure $p$ is defined as force per unit area: $p = \frac{F}{A}$. Show that the SI base units of the pascal ($\text{Pa}$) are $\text{kg m}^{-1}\text{ s}^{-2}$. [2]
(b) When a compressed gas expands by volume $\Delta V$ at constant pressure $p$, the work done $W$ by the gas is given by $W = p \Delta V$. Show that the expression $p \Delta V$ has the same SI base units as the joule ($\text{J}$). [2]
(c) The speed of sound $c$ in an ideal gas is modelled by the formula:
$c = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma p}{\rho}}$
where $p$ is gas pressure, $\rho$ is gas density, and $\gamma$ is a gas constant.
(i) Rearrange the equation to express $\gamma$ as the subject. [1]
(ii) By substituting SI base units, show that $\gamma$ is a dimensionless quantity (has no units). [1]

parts.description: Derive base units of pascal from F/A
Show base units of p Delta V match joule
Rearrange wave speed formula for gamma
Show gamma is dimensionless using base units

part_enrichment.guidance: Award M1 for (kg m s^-2) / m^2, and A1 for kg m^-1 s^-2.
Award M1 for (kg m^-1 s^-2) x m^3, and A1 for kg m^2 s^-2 with statement that this matches J.
part_enrichment.common_pitfalls: Forgetting that volume has units m^3.

part_enrichment.guidance: Award B1 for gamma = c^2 rho / p.
part_enrichment.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to square the speed c.

part_enrichment.guidance: Award B1 for showing [c^2 rho] = (m^2 s^-2)(kg m^-3) = kg m^-1 s^-2 which equals [p], so units cancel completely.

answer:
(a) [p] = [F]/[A] = (kg m s^-2) / m^2 = kg m^-1 s^-2
(b) [p Delta V] = (kg m^-1 s^-2)(m^3) = kg m^2 s^-2, which is identical to the base units of the joule (J).
(c)(i) gamma = c^2 rho / p
(c)(ii) [c^2 rho] = (m s^-1)^2 x (kg m^-3) = (m^2 s^-2)(kg m^-3) = kg m^-1 s^-2. Since [p] = kg m^-1 s^-2, [gamma] = (kg m^-1 s^-2) / (kg m^-1 s^-2) = 1 (no units).

mark_scheme.criterion: (b) Multiplies pressure base units by volume base units: (kg m^-1 s^-2) x m^3.
(b) Obtains kg m^2 s^-2 AND states that this is identical to the base-unit expression of the joule.
(c)(ii) Shows that [c^2 rho] = kg m^-1 s^-2, so [c^2 rho] / [p] cancels to 1 / dimensionless.

hints: In (a), force is kg m s^-2 and area is m^2.
In (b), volume Delta V is m^3. Multiply powers of m: -1 + 3 = 2.
In (c)(i), square both sides first to clear the square root.
In (c)(ii), substitute base units into the numerator and compare directly to the denominator.
solution:
(a) [p] = [F] / [A] = (kg m s^-2) / m^2 = kg x m^(1 - 2) x s^-2 = kg m^-1 s^-2.
(b) [W] = [p] x [Delta V] = (kg m^-1 s^-2) x m^3 = kg x m^(-1 + 3) x s^-2 = kg m^2 s^-2.
This is identical to the SI base units of work and energy (the joule, derived from W = Fd = N m = kg m^2 s^-2).
(c)(i) Squaring both sides: c^2 = (gamma p) / rho. Rearranging for gamma: gamma = (c^2 rho) / p.
(c)(ii) Base units of numerator:
[c^2 rho] = (m s^-1)^2 x (kg m^-3) = (m^2 s^-2) x (kg m^-3) = kg x m^(2 - 3) x s^-2 = kg m^-1 s^-2.
Base units of denominator:
[p] = kg m^-1 s^-2.
Therefore:
[gamma] = (kg m^-1 s^-2) / (kg m^-1 s^-2) = 1. All base units cancel, confirming that gamma is dimensionless.
teacher_walkthrough: Connects fluid pressure to mechanical thermodynamics and acoustic wave equations.
Part (b) demonstrates that p Delta V is energetically equivalent to Fd.
Part (c) demonstrates algebraic squaring of radical expressions and rigorous dimensional cancellation.

provenance.abstract_pattern: gas thermodynamics and acoustic wave speed dimensional analysis
